summary: Yellowstone National Park is America's premier geothermal wonderland, featuring the iconic Old Faithful geyser, stunning thermal features, and abundant wildlife across vast wilderness landscapes. Spanning three states, this UNESCO World Heritage site offers unparalleled photography opportunities, hiking trails, and immersive nature experiences that attract nearly four million visitors annually.

restaurants.name: Old Faithful Inn Dining Room
restaurants.description: Historic 1904 restaurant with views of Old Faithful, serving classic American comfort food and regional specialties. A legendary dining experience with architectural charm and reliable cuisine.

restaurants.name: Mammoth Hot Springs Hotel Dining Room
restaurants.description: Fine dining establishment within the park featuring locally-sourced ingredients and elevated comfort food. Offers views of the Mammoth Hot Springs terraces.

restaurants.name: Canyon Lodge Eatery
restaurants.description: Casual quick-service restaurant offering burgers, sandwiches, and pizza for families. Perfect for refueling between park activities.

restaurants.name: Lake Yellowstone Hotel Deli
restaurants.description: Casual deli counter serving sandwiches, salads, and grab-and-go options for day-trippers and hikers. Convenient and affordable.

restaurants.name: Roosevelt Lodge Roughrider Bar & Grill
restaurants.description: Rustic lodge restaurant with a Western frontier atmosphere, serving steaks, ribs, and hearty regional fare. Family-friendly with outdoor barbecue options.

restaurants.name: Norris Geyser Basin Picnic Area
restaurants.description: Free picnic facilities throughout the park with scenic overlooks where visitors can bring their own food. Enhances outdoor dining experiences near thermal features.

restaurants.name: West Yellowstone Eats & Treats
restaurants.description: Local favorite just outside the park offering burgers, local pastries, and casual comfort food in a small-town setting. Great value and authentic charm.

restaurants.name: Gardiner Park Restaurant
restaurants.description: Located at the North Entrance, featuring regional American cuisine with emphasis on local game and produce. Provides excellent views of the surrounding valleys.

restaurants.name: Old West Pizza Company
restaurants.description: Casual pizzeria in gateway towns serving wood-fired pizza and local craft beers. Popular with families and outdoor enthusiasts.

restaurants.name: Snake River Grill
restaurants.description: Upscale dining establishment in Jackson, Wyoming featuring contemporary American cuisine with Rocky Mountain influences. Reservations essential.

restaurants.name: Yellowstone Village Restaurant
restaurants.description: Family-style dining in gateway community offering hearty portions and regional specialties. Welcoming atmosphere for park visitors.

restaurants.name: Beartooth Cafe
restaurants.description: Local coffee shop and bakery in Red Lodge, Montana serving excellent coffee and freshly baked pastries. Ideal morning stop before park visits.

activities.name: Old Faithful Geyser Viewing
activities.description: Witness the eruption of Yellowstone's most famous geyser, shooting water up to 180 feet in the air. Eruptions occur approximately every 90 minutes with predictable timing.

activities.name: Grand Prismatic Spring Walk
activities.description: Explore the largest hot spring in the USA with brilliant blue center and rainbow-colored mineral deposits. The elevated boardwalk offers stunning views of this geothermal masterpiece.

activities.name: Lamar Valley Wildlife Safari
activities.description: Experience the American Serengeti with opportunities to spot bison, elk, wolves, and grizzly bears in their natural habitat. Early morning and evening drives offer the best wildlife viewing.

activities.name: Mammoth Hot Springs Terraces Hike
activities.description: Walk among the otherworldly white travertine terraces formed by mineral-rich hot water cascading down mountainsides. Multiple boardwalk options from easy to moderately challenging.

activities.name: Norris Geyser Basin Exploration
activities.description: Discover the hottest and most geothermally active basin in Yellowstone with colorful hot springs and regular geyser eruptions. Miles of boardwalks provide safe access to geothermal features.

activities.name: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone Viewpoints
activities.description: Marvel at 1,200-foot canyon walls and powerful waterfalls including the stunning Lower Falls plunging 308 feet. Multiple viewpoints and trails offer varying levels of difficulty.

activities.name: Backcountry Hiking to Remote Geyser
activities.description: Challenge yourself with a rigorous hike to less-visited geothermal areas like Shoshone Geyser Basin or Fountain Paint Pot. Rewards include solitude and pristine geothermal landscapes.

activities.name: Fly Fishing on Yellowstone Waters
activities.description: Cast for native cutthroat and rainbow trout in the pristine rivers and streams of Yellowstone with experienced guides. Requires fishing license and specific regulations adherence.

activities.name: Yellowstone Lake Boat Tour
activities.description: Cruise across North America's largest high-elevation lake with interpretive ranger commentary about geology and wildlife. Seasonal tours depart from Lake Village.

activities.name: Artist Point Sunset Experience
activities.description: Visit the iconic overlook of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone during golden hour for spectacular photography and painting opportunities. Arrive early to secure viewing spots.

activities.name: Mud Volcano and Sulphur Caldron Loop Trail
activities.description: Walk among bubbling mud pots, steaming vents, and colorful mineral deposits in this accessible thermal area. Easy boardwalk provides close encounters with geothermal activity.

activities.name: Ranger-Led Educational Programs
activities.description: Join free ranger-guided walks, campfire talks, and interpretive programs explaining Yellowstone's geology, ecology, and history. Programs vary seasonally and by location.

spots.name: Old Faithful at Sunrise
spots.description: Capture the geyser erupting against a golden sky with morning mist creating dramatic atmospheric effects.

spots.name: Grand Prismatic Spring Overlook
spots.description: Photograph the stunning blue center and rainbow-hued mineral deposits from the elevated boardwalk viewpoint.

spots.name: Lamar Valley Wildlife Corridor
spots.description: Capture bison, elk, wolves, and bears in their natural habitat against dramatic valley backdrops.

spots.name: Mammoth Hot Springs Terraces
spots.description: Document the otherworldly white travertine formations with mineral-colored pools and geothermal features.
spots.bestTime: Early morning for shadows and detail

spots.name: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone - Artist Point
spots.description: Capture iconic views of the canyon's 1,200-foot walls, the Lower Falls, and dramatic geological formations.

spots.name: Norris Geyser Basin Steam Vents
spots.description: Photograph ethereal steam rising from colorful hot springs and active geysers throughout the basin.
spots.bestTime: Early morning when steam is most dramatic

spots.name: Firehole Lake Drive Thermal Features
spots.description: Capture diverse geothermal phenomena including hot springs, mud pots, and mineral deposits in close proximity.

spots.name: Tower Fall Waterfall
spots.description: Photograph the 132-foot cascade surrounded by distinctive columnar basalt formations in a forested setting.

spots.name: Hayden Valley Bison Herd
spots.description: Document large herds of American bison grazing against mountain backdrops and golden grasslands.

spots.name: Morning Glory Pool Reflection
spots.description: Capture the vibrant blue hot spring's perfect reflections in calm morning conditions with surrounding forest.

lensRecommendations: 16-35mm wide-angle for expansive geothermal landscape vistas and canyon panoramas
70-200mm telephoto for wildlife isolation and distant mountain detail shots
50mm prime for intimate thermal feature photography and human-scale compositions
14mm ultra-wide for immersive sunrise/sunset and geothermal steam scenarios
photography.goldenHourNotes: Golden hour lighting dramatically transforms Yellowstone's geothermal features, illuminating steam and mineral deposits with warm hues. Early mornings offer the most dramatic steam effects and clearest atmospheric conditions, while late afternoon provides warm canyon wall illumination. Sunset at Artist Point consistently delivers exceptional color gradations across the canyon landscape.

weather.seasonality: Summer (June-September) offers warm weather, full road access, and peak wildlife activity, though crowds are substantial. Winter (December-March) provides pristine snow photography and thermal features, but extreme cold and limited road access challenge visitors.
weather.summary: Yellowstone experiences significant seasonal variation due to its high elevation (7,000-11,000 feet), with cold winters featuring heavy snow and mild summers with comfortable temperatures. Spring and fall serve as transition periods with unpredictable weather patterns and fewer visitors.

hotels.name: Old Faithful Inn
hotels.description: Historic 1904 grand lodge featuring iconic log architecture, authentic period charm, and convenient central park location with on-site dining and visitor facilities.

hotels.name: Mammoth Hot Springs Hotel
hotels.description: Comfortable lodge-style accommodations near the park's North Entrance with access to terraces, dining, and ranger programs in a quieter setting.

hotels.name: Lake Yellowstone Hotel & Cabins
hotels.description: Premier waterfront resort featuring historic hotel rooms and modern cabins with fine dining, lake views, boat tours, and upscale amenities in a serene location.
